scenario.name: campus
scenario.description: Campus LAN: three buildings inside 400 m, 1,600 endpoints, PoE access points, Cat6a access and OM4 backbone.

media.reason: Selected Cat6a copper with a 10GBASE-T transceiver because the access run (90 m) is within the 100 m 10GBASE-T channel limit (IEEE 802.3an). Category 6a supports 10 Gb/s over 100 m and is the lowest-cost medium at this distance.

Selected OM4 multimode fiber because the backbone run (320 m): it exceeds the 100 m Cat6a limit and stays inside the 400 m reach of 10GBASE-SR at 850 nm (IEEE 802.3ae). Modal dispersion limits multimode reach, so the design stays within the 400 m OM4 catalogue distance.

topology.reason: Selected three-tier because endpoints (1600) are >= 1000 or buildings (3) are >= 4. The design uses 34 access switch(es) at 48 ports each, 3 distribution switch(es), and 2 core switch(es). Oversubscription is (48 x 1 Gb/s) / (2 x 10 Gb/s) = 2.4:1.
advantages: Fault domains and broadcast domains stay small.
Distribution switches summarise routes and enforce policy.
Core links can be sized and upgraded independently.
disadvantages: More switches and more cabling than a collapsed core.
More OSPF adjacencies and more configuration surface.
tradeoffs: Higher capital cost; cleaner growth path and predictable convergence.
topology.cost_note: Cost was not scored because the scenario did not supply all three switch prices.

routing.reason: Selected single-area OSPF Area 0 because the scenario has one site, one autonomous system, 5 subnets (< 50), and no inter-site link longer than 400 m. A single link-state area converges quickly and keeps the design simple (RFC 2328).
alternatives: IS-IS is a link-state alternative, but OSPF is the Cisco-native choice for this course and Packet Tracer.

switching.reason: RSTP (IEEE 802.1w) is sufficient: 5 VLAN(s) <= 16 and 39 switch(es) < 50. Rapid PVST+ gives sub-second convergence per VLAN and Packet Tracer accepts it directly. HSRP is configured because the scenario is resilient: two cores share a virtual gateway, the first core uses priority 110, the second 100, and preemption returns traffic after a failure. VRRP (RFC 5798) is the open alternative. Trunk hardening: allowed VLANs 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, native VLAN 999.
hardening: Every trunk lists allowed VLAN ids explicitly; 'switchport trunk allowed vlan all' is never emitted.
Native VLAN is 999 and is not in the allowed user list.
Access ports enable PortFast and BPDU Guard.
Management VTY lines accept SSH only and are filtered by an ACL.

decisions.reason: Selected Cat6a copper with a 10GBASE-T transceiver because the access run (90 m) is within the 100 m 10GBASE-T channel limit (IEEE 802.3an). Category 6a supports 10 Gb/s over 100 m and is the lowest-cost medium at this distance.

Allocated 5 subnets inside 10.10.0.0/16 by sorting host requests largest-first and aligning each block to its own power-of-two boundary. 1600 requested hosts occupy 2304 addresses (69.4% address utilisation, 69.7% of usable addresses). device_configs.campus-core1:
! NetArchitect generated configuration
! Device: campus-core1
! Role: Layer-3 core switch
! Scenario: campus
! Lab credentials only; see README. Do not reuse in production.
!
hostname campus-core1
!
no ip domain-lookup
service timestamps debug datetime msec
service timestamps log datetime msec
!
enable secret NetArchitect-Lab-123
username admin privilege 15 secret NetArchitect-Lab-123
!
ip routing
!
! --- VLAN database ---
vlan 10
 name DATA
vlan 20
 name VOICE
vlan 30
 name WI-FI
vlan 40
 name MANAGEMENT
vlan 50
 name SERVERS
!
! --- Trunk to distribution 1 ---
interface GigabitEthernet1/0/1
 switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q
 switchport mode trunk
 switchport trunk native vlan 999
 switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,30,40,50
 no shutdown
!
! --- Trunk to distribution 2 ---
interface GigabitEthernet1/0/2
 switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q
 switchport mode trunk
 switchport trunk native vlan 999
 switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,30,40,50
 no shutdown
!
! --- Trunk to distribution 3 ---
interface GigabitEthernet1/0/3
 switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q
 switchport mode trunk
 switchport trunk native vlan 999
 switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,30,40,50
 no shutdown
!
! --- Data ---
interface Vlan10
 description Data
 ip address 10.10.0.2 255.255.252.0
 standby 10 ip 10.10.0.1
 standby 10 priority 110
 standby 10 preempt
 no shutdown
!
! --- Wi-Fi ---
interface Vlan30
 description Wi-Fi
 ip address 10.10.4.2 255.255.254.0
 standby 30 ip 10.10.4.1
 standby 30 priority 110
 standby 30 preempt
 no shutdown
!
! --- Voice ---
interface Vlan20
 description Voice
 ip address 10.10.6.2 255.255.254.0
 standby 20 ip 10.10.6.1
 standby 20 priority 110
 standby 20 preempt
 no shutdown
!
! --- Management ---
interface Vlan40
 description Management
 ip address 10.10.8.2 255.255.255.128
 standby 40 ip 10.10.8.1
 standby 40 priority 110
 standby 40 preempt
 no shutdown
!
! --- Servers ---
interface Vlan50
 description Servers
 ip address 10.10.8.130 255.255.255.128
 standby 50 ip 10.10.8.129
 standby 50 priority 110
 standby 50 preempt
 no shutdown
!
!
spanning-tree mode rapid-pvst
spanning-tree vlan 10,20,30,40,50 priority 4096
!
! --- OSPF ---
router ospf 1
 router-id 10.10.8.2
 network 10.10.0.0 0.0.3.255 area 0
 network 10.10.4.0 0.0.1.255 area 0
 network 10.10.6.0 0.0.1.255 area 0
 network 10.10.8.0 0.0.0.127 area 0
 network 10.10.8.128 0.0.0.127 area 0
 passive-interface Vlan10
 passive-interface Vlan30
 passive-interface Vlan20
 passive-interface Vlan40
 passive-interface Vlan50
!
ip access-list extended MGMT-ACCESS
 permit tcp 10.10.8.0 0.0.0.127 any eq 22
 deny ip any any
!
ip access-list extended GUEST-ISOLATION
 deny ip 10.10.4.0 0.0.1.255 10.10.8.128 0.0.0.127
 permit ip any any
!
interface Vlan30
 ip access-group GUEST-ISOLATION in
!
line con 0
 logging synchronous
line vty 0 4
 login local
 transport input ssh
 access-class MGMT-ACCESS in
!
end
